what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: Find the fifth of answers that vanish before anything is ranked
agents.why: Even if we showed the AI every fund it could possibly see, one founder in five would still not have theirs on the list. That is a hard ceiling of 77%, and it sits above everything else — no amount of improving the chooser can pass it. This decides whether reaching 90% is a plumbing job or means buying more of Europe's funding landscape, which are very different plans.

agents.what: Understand the cut from seventy-odd funds to eighteen
agents.why: The shortlist is trimmed to eighteen before the AI sees it, and that trim is where most of the loss happens. Nobody knows why it is eighteen; the likeliest answer is a cost limit from when asking the AI was expensive. The one thing already ruled out is simply raising it — that was tried and made the answer worse.

We have four different accuracy figures, each measured on a different set of founders. Twice today I compared two of them and drew a conclusion that was wrong. Steering towards 90% on numbers that are not on the same scale produces confident nonsense, so every stage is being re-measured one way, for free, repeatably.

agents.what: Free up the laptop, and move what belongs in the cloud
agents.why: The machine is at 99% full, which stops work outright. Sixteen finished branches have already been cleared, freeing over a gigabyte. The rest is working out which of the local data is genuinely a copy of something already safe on Railway — proven, not assumed, because we found work today that existed in exactly one place.
